items.title: Joe Robichaux Interview, 1959-03-19
items.q: Ridgely hired Don Albert and Contrell to work with him... So Don Albert recorded after me. He recorded the same tune with his big band.

ctx.x: Yeah, it's the same thing. You see that was a tune, I think it was Feynman's son was going up to Tulane. And it was his number. And he told Celestad's band that he had this number and anything they could do with it, you know, they could have it. And so John Porter, the bass player, he was hunting and he wrote the lead of it down. And saying he gave them the words. And they began to play it because Celestad and Ridgely band was, they were together then. Yeah. And so finally he wrote it, they wrote it down and they…
Yeah, they didn't know who to pay it to I guess.

items.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03
items.q: Even though Joe had quite a reputation with his family.

ctx.x: I see. I haven't got nothing mixed up. I don't know if you meant Joe or John. Mm-hmm. Well, John was all right.

Tanglefoot is simple. That's what I'm like. Pigeon Joe is one. Mm-hmm. That's what I'm saying. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, boy. Look at this nippy. He's a great dad. But I know when people talk about Robichaud today, very often they mean the old man, John, the left-handed bomb. Yeah. Even though Joe had quite a reputation with his family. Yeah.
And they still say John Robichaud. And they talk about Robichaud.
